Relocatable layout

Status: accepted, 2026-10-25; amended the same day to preserve main's uid, directory and installation rules.

  1. MixOS asks for installation roots rather than embedding locations. Existing environment names and per-caller directory policies are retained.
  2. Canonical roots are prefix, share, etc, var, run, cache. etc, var, run and share preserve the rules of libs/config/src/dir.rs at 32650ae5: MIXOS_ETC, MIXOS_VAR, MIXOS_RUN, MIXOS_SHARE and whole-tree MIXOS; real uid 0 means system, other uids mean user/XDG. Relative XDG values are ignored. Var uses XDG data, and run keeps the /tmp/mixos-run fallback. Only the installed prefix and default share location change to self-location. Cache is additive. Caller-owned app state and per-file overrides keep their own rules.
  3. Per-root precedence is its override, then $MIXOS where applicable, then <prefix>/layout.mx, then uid defaults. Share ignores $MIXOS and accepts only an absolute override. Prefix comes from MIXOS_PREFIX, else canonical /proc/self/exe and the parent of bin/; it never selects tier. The bounded strict-data layout has at most etc, var, run, share, cache, and refuses a prefix key. The paths manual gives the complete table and explicit system/user APIs. A root stored in layout.mx applies to every uid, like $MIXOS. Installers persist only differences from the system defaults for the target prefix; the default installation has no layout.mx and preserves each user's XDG roots.
  4. libs/paths owns the implementation without workspace dependencies; config::dir re-exports the original API. Rust and mixos_path share it. Process helpers resolve once; pure explicit inputs support tests.
  5. External files use @{prefix}, @{share}, @{etc}, @{var}, @{run}, @{cache}. mix layout apply renders idempotently and prints changes. Templates render to the existing packaged places inside the prefix: share/<component>/units/, share/applications/ and other shipped paths. Template sources remain with their components and ship in share/layout. Gold renders while staging, before hashing and recording receipt bytes. Enabling services remains the operator's step. Layout apply never installs systemd, sysusers, tmpfiles or polkit files outside the prefix and never touches unmanaged flat share/units/ copies. Mix component units remain owned and rendered by component_install, outside the global manifest. Only the ruling 9 link and, on a host, its line in /etc/shells are managed outside the prefix. There is no mixrc management. With --root, /etc/shells is touched only inside that root and only with --image, which requires --root. The root is canonicalised; symlinks below it and symlink render targets refuse. All targets are checked for writability before writing; existing modes and owners are preserved, and new rendered files are 0644. Paths containing whitespace refuse in systemd keys that do not unquote (including EnvironmentFile, ConditionPathExists and LoadCredential).
  6. Saved MixOS references use mixos:<root>/<relative>. Root escapes refuse; user-owned paths retain their meaning. Offline migration keeps originals; live migration is a separate operator action.
  7. The path gate joins lint. Literal defaults are limited to the resolver, external templates, default assertions and documentation. Shipped scripts use #!/usr/bin/env mix or are invoked with Mix. The behaviour-preservation review explicitly permits deferring a literal where a replacement cannot be proved equivalent. Three fixed-FHS Mix fallbacks and two storage-path lines in indexd's example are recorded by exact file, line and reason in tools/path_gate_exceptions.mx; stale entries or additional occurrences fail the gate. They are not a general path fallback or an environment alias.
  8. Main's directory tests move with unchanged assertions. A table compares each root under public-safe desktop, system-unit and bare-login environments for uid 0 and a user at both default and moved prefixes. No default-layout user data moves are accepted. The relocation proof uses a disposable prefix with a space and hides the old roots in a private mount namespace; it runs installer, scene, nested desktop and SSH loopback checks where available. Missing privileges are reported as skips.
  9. The stable host entry is /usr/local/bin/mix; /usr/bin/mix is managed only in a MixOS-owned image. Login shells and /etc/shells use that link. mix-static stays unlinked. Remote lookup is option, environment, per-host table when one exists, then mix on PATH.

N-1 tooling remains usable before a new binary is installed. Installers get target defaults by invoking the verified staged binary's mix layout defaults command. They do not select a target from their own interpreter. Rollback can read the receipt or target layout without running the installed target. Main receipts with an absolute target and backup and no layout are read in their original shape; the absent layout means the default layout. Their recorded prefix and var backup path suffice for offline rollback. They also participate in release ordering alongside logical receipts.

This decision does not deploy or migrate a live installation, move app data, introduce hot relocation, generations or a versioned store.
